lines.text: This is MARSAD one, Team Kanban's three U CubeSat for spotting harmful algal blooms off the UAE coast.
On the bench: an ESP thirty two S3 flight computer, a spectral sensor, a camera and a LoRa radio.
Every second it reads power, temperature and light, and decides what the satellite should do.
After separation, a servo releases the tape antenna.
The payload compares red and near infrared light to flag water thick with algae.
Here is that flight logic running in simulation. Green means imaging.
Five seconds after boot, the antenna deploys.
Every ten seconds, a ground pass lights the downlink LED, and every reading streams out as JSON.
That JSON feeds our mission control dashboard. We inject faults to test it.
A drained battery turns the tiles red and forces safe mode. A cold battery trips the heater alarm.
When the link drops, every value goes grey and stale, then link lost.
Clear the faults, and it recovers on its own.
Same code, same data, from the bench to orbit.
